By interest

How to choose a gift for a reader

Choose books, reading lights, journals, and collectibles around their reading habits and existing collection.

By Couple Better Gifts · Updated October 26, 2026 · How we choose gifts

On this page

  1. Buying a book: check the title and edition
  2. Reading accessories: picture where they will use it
  3. Choose a light for their reading spot
  4. Look inside a journal
  5. Buying character merchandise

Find out what they read, how they read, and what they already own. A reader who listens to audiobooks may have little use for a clip-on book light. Someone who collects hardcovers may care about the exact edition of a favorite novel.

Buying a book: check the title and edition

Start with a book they have mentioned wanting or a gap in a series they collect. Check the author, title, format, and edition. Compare the cover and dimensions with their existing books if they like a matching set. For a translated book, check the translator too.

Ask whether they already own it, have borrowed it, or plan to buy a particular edition. A signed or illustrated edition can be appealing when you know that preference. Read the seller’s description of what makes the edition different before paying extra.

Reading accessories: picture where they will use it

GiftWho it could suitWhat to check
Clip-on reading lightSomeone who reads paper books in low light.Attachment, weight, beam direction, and charging.
Wearable neck lightSomeone who prefers a light carried on their body.Weight, adjustment, controls, and comfort.
Reading journalSomeone who enjoys recording books or quotes.Sample pages and room for their usual notes.
Bookmark or shelf keepsakeSomeone with a favorite series or character.Design, materials, and available display space.

Choose a light for their reading spot

Look at the chair, bed, or desk where they usually read. A clip-on design needs a suitable place to attach. A wearable light adds weight around the neck. Compare the product’s position in photos with the way the recipient holds a book.

For someone who reads beside a sleeping partner, look for directional adjustment and accessible brightness controls. Check the charging method and whether the necessary cable or power supply is included.

Look inside a journal

Structured prompts can help someone keep short, consistent entries. Open pages allow longer thoughts, sketches, and quotes. Read the sample pages before choosing a format. If they already track reading in an app, ask whether they would enjoy a paper journal as well.

Buying character merchandise

Confirm the character and maker. For a series such as The Stormlight Archive, check the maker’s own licensing information and buy from a seller you can identify. Measure the shelf space for a figure or book nook, and check whether assembly, tools, or lighting supplies are required.

Include a short note about the book you discussed or the character they love. That connection can make a small gift feel considered.
